Reliable financial information shapes decisions, protects businesses, and helps them act with confidence. That is what drew me to financial accounting: the satisfaction of turning complex numbers into a clear, trustworthy story that helps people make confident decisions. I am from India and hold a Bachelor’s degree from a university not listed in the major global rankings, and that academic foundation, together with completing 3 projects with tangible outcomes, has strengthened my interest in work where accuracy, structure, and practical impact matter. My perspective on the profession has also been shaped by seeing how much progress depends on clarity in an organisation’s finances. While reporting is essential, I believe the most valuable part of financial accounting is the process of spotting patterns and discrepancies early so that reporting can be adjusted without losing sight of the underlying figures.

That approach has been tested in practice. In one role, I needed to use a technique that was new to me, so I learned it within a couple of months and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another occasion, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work continue more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on before, and I value those moments because they reflect the importance of clear communication and dependable follow-through. I also took the initiative to begin a substantial piece of work beyond my formal role and carried it through over many months until it was completed.

What keeps this career personal for me is how naturally it connects with everyday life. During a family dinner, I once settled a lighthearted debate about splitting holiday costs by building a simple spreadsheet on the spot; it became the template my family still uses for events, and it reminded me how naturally accounting can turn uncertainty into a plan. I am now eager to bring this same care, structure, and practical judgement to a Financial Accountant role where I can contribute to reliable reporting, compliance, and a clear financial picture.

Few things are more rewarding than watching a child move from uncertainty to understanding, and that is what drew me towards becoming a Primary School Teacher. Inspired by the way great teachers can shape a child’s confidence as much as their academic progress, I chose primary education to help children discover curiosity, resilience, and a genuine love of learning from the very start. I am originally from Colombia, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100. Through my studies and professional development, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in turning complex ideas into engaging, age-appropriate lessons that invite participation from children with different learning styles. One of my favourite memories is of a family member visiting the classroom and watching a younger family member proudly use their very first kit at an event I had helped organise, then ask me to recommend “a great kit for a school project.” That moment captured exactly why this profession matters to me.

In practice, I have seen how progress often depends on making learning accessible and purposeful. When I needed to use a new digital teaching tool and become familiar with a new subject area, I did not master it all at once; instead, I built confidence through steady use over more than a year until it became part of my routine. In another role, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time at the same stage of a project, so I introduced a simple adjustment to the process that reduced delays and saved time across the week. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on, and I value those moments because they reflect the collaborative side of teaching. I also volunteered for a major undertaking outside my formal duties and continued it alongside my regular work for over a year until it was completed. Altogether, these experiences have prepared me to contribute thoughtfully and grow into a Primary School Teacher who brings clear communication, creativity, and a genuine commitment to helping children grow in understanding.

My background has also shaped the way I approach technical work. I am especially drawn to the discipline required to keep records, equipment, and results accurate, so that results are dependable, well-interpreted, and usable in everyday settings. On another occasion, I noticed a recurring bottleneck in the team’s process and introduced a simple fix that reduced repeated delays and saved time. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on before, and I value those exchanges because they keep technical work collaborative.

Alongside my regular responsibilities, I also volunteered for a major undertaking outside my formal duties and continued with it for more than a year until it was completed. Experiences like these have strengthened my ability to work carefully under pressure, maintain accuracy under tight deadlines, and contribute to reliable results that support wider team goals. I am now eager to bring that same care, consistency, and practical focus to a Laboratory Technician position where accurate testing and dependable documentation matter every day.
